messages:
Alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection heuristics rollout at 02:15 UTC we saw a sharp drop in prefix cache hit rate for a subset of customers. Investigating.
Mira: graphs? rough numbers?
Alex: overall hit-rate fell from ~92% -> ~64% on the affected pool. Latency tail rose ~120ms p99 on short prompts.
Kevin: Did the rollout change cache keying semantics or include any extra request metadata? That looks like an entropy jump.
Alex: We changed the kernel selection to include sequence-length-bucket and a new session affinity token in routing decisions. I only meant routing, not the cache key — but checking now.
Jordan: ops-bot fired an alert around the same time: "cache-miss-surge: prefetchevaluator backend saturating". I'll paste the alert log.
ops-bot: ALERT: cache-prefetch-queue-depth > 5000 on pool-west-2 for 3m; downstream error-rate 4.3%.
Mira: sample logs show a lot of varying key tails: keys now look like `prefix|model-v2|len:32|session:abcd1234` instead of `prefix|model-v2|len:32`. That extra session token will make the same prefixes miss.
Kevin: Ohhh — session token was accidentally wired into CacheKeyBuilder when we merged the kernel selector branch. Config diff:
```
- key = f"{prefix}|{model}"
+ key = f"{prefix}|{model}|len:{bucket}|session:{session_id}"
```
Jordan: So each call with new ephemeral session_id explodes keyspace — stampede on warmups.
Alex: Reproduced locally: with session in key hit-rate drops from 90%->18% on small prompt distribution.
Mira: What's the emergency plan? Roll back the merge and throttle prefetches?
Kevin: Short-term: revert keying change and add aggressive backoff on prefetch worker concurrency. Medium: add unit tests to catch non-deterministic key components, and add a canary to prefetch rate.
Jordan: I've queued a rollback of the keying change to canary pool. Will monitor hit-rate.
ops-bot: NOTE: rollback job started (ci/rollout 4821) — estimated 2m.
Alex: After rollback to old KeyBuilder (no session) hit-rate on canary went to 91% within 90s. Prefetch queue drained.
Mira: Did kernel selection change still remain? We need kernel heuristics without polluting cache keys.
Kevin: Yes — kernel routing intact. We refactored so kernel selector emits a routing tag, but we removed session from cache key. Patch snippet:
```
- cache_key_components.add(session_id)
+ cache_key_components.add(routing_tag)
```
Jordan: Added a test that exercises generating cache key across 1000 synthetic sessions verifying dedup rate > 80%.
Alex: Also added a prefetch backoff: if miss-rate > 30% and queue-depth growing, exponentially backoff prefetch concurrency and fall back to on-demand cold-starts for 30s.
Mira: Good. Any perf regressions from kernel selection itself? Were we tripping a slower kernel for short sequences?
Kevin: Profiling shows no meaningful kernel slowdown; p50 token throughput same. The latency tail came from increased cold starts and KV service overload due to miss storm.
Jordan: Action items: (1) Roll forward rollback to prod if canary stable (Alex/Jordan). (2) Add CI guard against ephemeral ids in keys (Kevin). (3) Add prefetch backoff + telemetry (Mira). (4) Postmortem with customer impact summary (Alex).
Alex: Can confirm canary stable for 12m, rolling to prod in 10m window. Will post postmortem draft afterwards.
Mira: Nice catch — :eyes: good call on pairing kernel change with keying review.
Kevin: We should also add a lint in CacheKeyBuilder that raises on inclusion of fields labeled 'ephemeral' or 'session'.
ops-bot: INFO: prod rollout started (ci/rollout 4822). Monitor: /alerts/cache-miss-surge ; /dashboards/prefetch-queue.
Jordan: Closing thread; will reopen if any regression. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
